# Generic and dormant evidence: first study

These two archives preserve every byte of the new six-case first-source packet
and its fourteen actual CLI checks, including the original predictions,
uncertainty, driver, diagnostics, raw streams, complete input inventory and final
audit. This is an informed study, not a blind benchmark. Earlier authoring
packets remain unchanged.

| [First observations](first-observations.tar.gz) | 50 | 3,978,071 | 734,423 |
| **Total** | **70** | **4,044,578** | **754,125** |

[The complete manifest](packets.json) binds every original path, size, SHA-256

the observation freeze is

Authoring-time `executed=false` labels remain original history; the separate

## Actual checks and their limits

All fourteen literal checks ran once: **3 acceptances / 11 refusals / 0 timeouts**.
Every prediction matched, including C's explicitly uncertain acceptance prediction.
There were no runs, emissions, retries, source repairs or fallback requests.

| Case | Finite | Selected Raw |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A: generic identity at Unit/Bit/Bits0/full product trees, forwarding alias and local shadow | Unsupported static-argument profile | Accepted |
| B: generic structural reversal with separate A/B | Unsupported static-argument profile | Accepted |
| C: harmless main with false Meaning requests in unused generic bodies | Unsupported opaque Basis profile | Accepted for selected main only |
| D: closed false X-versus-Z Meaning under adjoint/zero power | Contract refusal | Contract refusal |
| E: Nat helper and intermediate-u32 overflow, fixed one-Bit data | Unsupported static Nat profile | Limit refusal |
| F: imported public Observe provider with an H body supplied as pure Op | Common effect refusal | Common effect refusal |

Two separately predeclared selected controls bind C's actual `unused_binding`
and `unused_zero` helpers with `A=Unit`; both receive genuine contract refusals.
The unused Op argument and zero-repeat child therefore retain their false
Meaning when selected. C's harmless-main validity is **not dormant Meaning discharge**.
Finite early profile refusals do not validate later instance, Meaning or arithmetic
obligations. The intended future contracts remain separately recorded in the
original source packet; this history does not implement them.

All three successful outputs explicitly report native-validity,
`request_checked=false`, `source_steps_checked=true`,
`source_meaning_verified=false` and `source_preservation_verified=false`.
Their native scope is selected-specialization; complete common source checking
does not turn unmaterialized generic evidence into an independent native check.
The execution authority is checked-produced-ir. Kernel identity in CLI JSON is
unpinned despite externally captured exact binary hashes.

Authored concrete interfaces use at most two physical qubits. E's large natural

#39/#63/qlippy/generic-QFT exclusions remain unchanged. No feature, Issue,
release, guarantee or constitutional adoption is completed by this study.

## Inert retention reader

Run `python3 -B scripts/test_generic_dormant_first.py` from the repository root.
It never executes recorded commands. It opens only current retained archives,
manifest and README; original external paths and executable identities are data.
It extracts no files and never imports an archived runner or source program.
The reader prebounds compressed bytes, expanded container/member bytes and counts,
then rejects unsafe, duplicate, nonregular and hidden PAX/GNU entries before
tarfile parses them. Fixed bounds are 2 MiB compressed, 5 MiB original content,
4 MiB per member and 80 members, with bounded container overhead.

Regular-only USTAR members are ordered by path components, with mode `0644`,
zero uid/gid/time and empty owner names; deterministic gzip has an empty filename
and zero timestamp. These are retention metadata, not historical Git provenance
or authentication of authorship. External originals were verified before and
after packaging. Repository fixture ceilings remain 150 MiB / 18,000 files /
100,000 added text lines. Fresh compiler studies require new commands and records.
